subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.**

The driver __lose control as soon as__ he was taking a right turn.
solution:
The correct answer is: **lost control when**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lost **means to no longer be in control of something. It is the base form of the verb (Verb1)
 
• **Lost **is simply the past tense of lose.
 
• "**As soon as**" is a conjunction and it's used when something happens immediately after some other event. We use **"as soon as...than"** in a sentence.
 
• We use '**when**' as a conjunction meaning **'at the time that'.**
 
• The clause with '**when**' is a subordinate clause (sc) and needs a main clause (mc) to complete its meaning.
 
• The given sentence is written in the past tense so '**Lost**' should be used, and both the actions occurred in the same time so, '**when**' should be used.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3** which is "lost control when"

Corrected sentence: *The driver **lost control when __**he was taking a right turn. *
